Prompt to build this component

When to use it

When to use

  • For one item in a vertical list: a person, a file, a step, a setting, a search result.
  • For a destination in a navigation list, with the compact variant (a sidebar or a menu).
  • When items are scanned top to bottom and each has a name, perhaps a leading icon or avatar, a line of detail and something at the end (a count, a status, a chevron).

When not to use

  • For items compared side by side in columns: use cmp-table.
  • For items with pictures that people browse: use cards in a grid.
  • For a single action: use cmp-button.
Variants, anatomy, accessibility, interaction and content rules

Variants

  • default — a content row with a hairline divider below it and inner padding on both sides; put rows in a flush card or a bare list so they run edge to edge. The base class alone; no modifier class.
  • compact — a navigation row: tighter, no divider, muted until hovered, and a raised highlight on the current destination.

Anatomy

  • Root: <div class="ds-list-row"> for a row that only shows content; <a class="ds-list-row"> or <button class="ds-list-row" type="button"> when the whole row acts. Put rows in a ul or ol (one li per row) when they form a list.
  • Leading (optional): <span class="ds-list-row__leading"> holding an icon (ds-icon) or, in a screen, an avatar.
  • Text: <span class="ds-list-row__text"> holding the item's name; it takes the free width and truncates in compact rows.
  • Meta (optional): <span class="ds-list-row__meta"> inside the text part, a second, muted line of detail.
  • Trailing (optional): <span class="ds-list-row__trailing"> at the end: a count, a short value, a status or a chevron-right icon.
  • Current: aria-current="page" (or "step", "true") on the row that is the current place.

Accessibility

  • A row that acts is a single link or button; it holds no other interactive element.
  • The current destination carries aria-current; it is shown by a raised highlight and strong weight, never by colour alone.
  • Icons in the leading part are decorative when the text names the item.
  • Every row is at least the minimum target tall, so it can be hit with a finger or a pointer.

Interaction

  • Rows that act fill with the sunken colour on hover within the quick duration; nothing moves (int-01, int-03).
  • Focus draws the shared ring inside the row, so it is never clipped by a card's edge, and stays on the row after it acts in place (int-02).
  • Becoming current eases its fill and colour within the quick duration, without animation of position; its weight changes at once (instant: a font weight does not animate) (int-04).

Content rules

  • Lead with the item's name, in sentence case; put dates, owners and counts in meta or trailing.
  • Keep compact rows to one or two words, and use the same names and order as everywhere else in the product.
  • Counts in trailing are numbers only; say what they count in the meta line or nearby heading.

Do and don't

  • Do keep leading parts the same kind (all icons or all avatars) within one list.
  • Do use the compact variant for every destination in a sidebar, with icons for top-level places.
  • Don't mix default and compact rows in one list.
  • Don't put a button inside a row that is itself a link; split the action into its own column or menu.
